mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity authority of the holder's state of nationality or residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of each individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent authority of the parent company's place of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors and officers against the Swiss SECO embargo lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic Swiss sanctions regulations under the Embargo Act (SR 946.231). Enhanced due diligence applies to foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates as required by AMLA arts. 2–9 and FINMA regulatory practice. For payroll payment rails using USD clearing, Swift wire transfers, and ACH Direct Debit, additional screening against the OFAC SDN List is adopted as institutional best practice. Ongoing monitoring is required while the entity engages in financial intermediary activities or holds client funds; otherwise the company must maintain appropriate CDD records in connection with all investor fund flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Swiss Central Business Company Names Index (www.zefix.ch); official name clearance is administered in advance by the canton-level Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) before notarization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin script. Names in the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) are freely accepted; foreign-language names are permitted if they are not misleading and can be transliterated or translated into a Swiss national language for the commercial register filing where the cantonal registrar requires clarity. The name must contain the legal form indicator 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG'; the abbreviation must correspond to the selected corporate form and appear in all registered formal names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca (requires FINMA banking licence)
Insurance / Assurance / Assicurazione (requires FINMA insurance supervisory licence)
Lawyer / Rechtsanwalt / Avocat / Avvocato (protected professional title, requires cantonal bar admission)
Notary / Notar / Notaire (protected professional title, requires notarial commission)
Trust (trustee or fiduciary title, requires applicable cantonal authorization and is scrutinized as misleading)
Swiss / Suisse / Schweiz / Confederation / Federal / Bund (suggests sovereign or governmental affiliation; requires prior federal/cantonal authorization or confirmation of non-misleading use)
International / Global / Export (scrutinized for misleading geographical substance)
SA / Ltd / LLC / GmbH / plc (inconsistent with the Swiss Aktiengesellschaft legal form and therefore rejected)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed company name by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the competent cantonal supervisory authority within 30 days of receipt of the written rejection. The appeal must state the legal grounds for the registrability of the name and may include rebuttal evidence of non-confusion or prior permissible use. If the cantonal supervisory authority rejects the appeal, the applicant may further appeal to the cantonal administrative court and, ultimately, to the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne on public law grounds. If the name is rejected but no formal appeal is pursued, the applicant may file a new application with an amended name or pursue renewal of a reservation before expiry of the 180-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or mail-forwarding-only address is not statutorily accepted as the sole registered seat of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office must be the actual administrative seat or a physical office identifiable in the canton of registration. A licensed domiciliation or corporate services provider can be used in most cantons, provided it maintains a real physical office at the registered address and the company can demonstrate adequate administrative substance. Highly vulnerable arrangements such as a letterbox office increase tax and commercial registry scrutiny and may be rejected by the registrar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection is estimated at 5–10% during the first three years of operations for a non-regulated payroll software AG. The most probable inspection authorities are cantonal tax offices, social security compensation offices, and audit authorities; if the company handles client funds or provides payment services, FINMA and AML compliance inspections become materially more likely and may include unannounced visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official commercial register fee schedule under HRegV

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations / Codice delle obbligazioni), SR 220, Articles 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft), as revised by the 2023 Swiss Stock Corporation Law Reform (Federal Act of 19 June 2020, in force 1 January 2023).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operating within the Federal Commercial Register Information System (Zefix) and supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office at the Federal Office of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration for Commercial Registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister / Déclaration de constitution au registre du commerce), accompanied by the notarized deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An Aktiengesellschaft must maintain a minimum share capital of CHF 100,000. Before registration, at least 20% of the nominal capital, subject to a floor of CHF 50,000, must be fully paid up in cash and held in a blocked (escrow) account with a Swiss bank; contributions in kind require a licensed statutory auditor's report and specific valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the share capital of CHF 100,000 has been fully subscribed, unanimously RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value is hereby approved and allocated to the incorporator; (2) the registered office of the company is adopted at Grabenstrasse 4, 6300 Zug, Switzerland; (3) [Name] is appointed Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer, with sole signature authority; (4) the paid-up portion of CHF 50,000, exceeding the statutory minimum, is confirmed as available in the blocked escrow account; (5) the Board authorizes the submission of the incorporation declaration to the Zug Commercial Register and instructs the officers to register the company for VAT and social insurance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Execution of the Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary of Zug (Notariat Zug), with mandatory pre-registration name screening through the Federal Commercial Register Index (Zefix).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of association (Statuten) containing the corporate name, registered seat in Zug, purpose limited to payroll software and SaaS services, share capital of CHF 100,000, board composition, and signatory rules. The incorporating shareholder personally attends a notarization session, signs the articles, and the notary authenticates the public deed. The notary then prepares the registration declaration annexed to the deed.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or landlord consent)
Beneficial ownership declaration under Swiss AML rules (GwG/AMLA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or name screening rejects the proposed corporate name, revise the name to eliminate risk of confusion with identical or similar protected names, obtain a fresh Zefix confirmation, and resubmit the articles for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of the Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank, including Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS Switzerland AG, issuing a blocked-account confirmation (Sperrbescheinigung / attestation de blocage).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an escrow account in the name of 'CH_AG in formation' and deposit not less than CHF 50,000 (20% of nominal capital and the statutory floor). Instruct the bank to block the funds and issue a written confirmation addressed to the notary and the Commercial Register Office that the amount is available solely for the company after the registration becomes effective.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed or articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening because the beneficial ownership file is incomplete, resubmit the full UBO documentation; if the bank refuses the blocked-account modality, engage another Swiss bank that accepts Sperrkonto arrangements and obtain a fresh blocking confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Verification and Formal Execution of the Notarial Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notariat Zug, assisted by a Swiss statutory auditor (RAB) only where contributions in kind are declared.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary examines the bank's blocked-account confirmation, verifies that paid-up capital equals at least CHF 50,000, certifies subscriptions, and formalizes the notarial incorporation deed together with the constitutive minutes. Where non-cash contributions are present, the statutory auditor's report on the valuation is attached to the deed.
required_dossiers: Constitutive minutes of the incorporation session
Statutory auditor's report for contributions in kind (if applicable)
Formal appointment acceptances of directors and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary query the provenance of the capital or completeness of the due diligence file, deliver the bank's AML statements and, where an audit report is defective, instruct the appointed auditor to issue a corrected opinion prior to execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to the Zug Commercial Register and Entry into the Official Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), electronically linked with the Federal Zefix registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed registration declaration, annexing the notarial deed, articles, bank confirmation, address proof, and director acceptance documents via the e-Register portal or directly at the registry counter. Pay the combined cantonal and federal fees. Following the review, the registry enters the company, publishes the entry in the Swiss Official Gazette, and issues the official commercial register extract incorporating the UID business number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal requisition regarding the corporate name, capital, address, or officer eligibility, cure through the notary by filing a corrective submission within the statutory response period; an unlawful refusal may be appealed to the cantonal supervisory authority and ultimately the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the UID Business Identifier and Value Added Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (Zefix/UID gateway) for the Enterprise Identification Number; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) through EasyGov for VAT (MWST/IVA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The UID is automatically generated after the commercial register entry. Apply for VAT via EasyGov within 30 days when annual revenue from payroll software subscriptions is expected to exceed CHF 100,000; the tax administration then issues the VAT number and determines the applicable domestic or foreign supplier treatment.
required_dossiers: UID confirmation from the Federal Statistical Office
Company name, seat, and actual business address
Forecast of turnover and place-of-supply analysis
Customer contract templates and SaaS revenue model description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not automatically created after register entry, request its issuance directly from the Federal Statistical Office using the official extract; if a VAT registration decision is disputed, file an objection with ESTV and subsequently with the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration for AHV/OASI, SUVA Accident Insurance, and Family Allowance Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse Zug), Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA), and the Cantonal Family Allowance Fund (Kantonale Familienausgleichskasse).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer and enroll all future directors, executives, and payroll employees in the Swiss old-age and survivors insurance (AHV/AVS) scheme. Conclude the compulsory occupational accident insurance contract with SUVA and register the payroll headcount with the family allowance fund; configure the payroll automation platform to submit monthly contribution statements using the UID.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the board and authorized signatories
Signed employer declaration for the AHV compensation office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office requests supplemental payroll or shareholder records, submit the amended declarations without delay; if SUVA's occupational risk category is contested for an office-based software company, apply for reclassification to the lower exposure group and settle retroactive contribution invoices accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing operation is established; the Cantonal Office for Economy and Labour of Zug (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit, AWA) retains general competence for permanent commercial occupation authorizations without requiring a special sectoral license for software services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No special operating business license (Sonderbewilligung) is mandated under Swiss federal or cantonal law for a pure payroll software and SaaS company; the commercial register entry, together with the municipal business notification, constitutes the lawful operation authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU), with the Zug Municipal Environment Authority for local waste and water permits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the project qualifies under the 'no project' category of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OPRO), because purely office-based IT activities produce no structural change, no land use alteration, and no material emission source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge streams are generated; if sanitary effluent is connected, compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV/OEaux), Annex 3.2 effluent quality standards, applies, and any standby generator must satisfy the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV/OPair) emission limits with a low-NOx specification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety clearance certificate from the Zug Fire Safety Police (Feuerpolizei Zug) based on office occupancy load and evacuation routes; provide a structural load assessment of the rented premises; and complete the workplace inspection required under the Swiss Labor Act (ArG) and the SUVA occupational health and risk evaluation under Article 82 UVG, including first-aid provisions and evacuation instructions for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC/FTA) — www.estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax authorities via SwissTax (www.suisse-tax.ch) and the Federal Tax Administration's portal for VAT (www.imea.admin.ch)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Swiss AG must first obtain a Swiss Company Identification Number (UID) from the Federal Statistical Office's UID register (www.uid.ch) via the commercial register entry; the UID serves as the VAT number and employer identification. For VAT, the company must complete the electronic VAT registration form (Formulaire 764) on the ESTV's e-service portal (www.imea.admin.ch) or via the SwissTax portal, providing the UID, business purpose, and estimated turnover. The cantonal tax administration automatically issues the corporate income tax master data after commercial register registration. A foreign entity without a Swiss permanent establishment but engaging in taxable activities in Switzerland must register for VAT through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using a foreign-entity UID application, if turnover exceeds CHF 100,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election exists under Swiss tax law; Swiss AGs are per se corporations subject to corporate income tax at the federal, cantonal, and communal levels. However, VAT grouping (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) election is available for closely linked Swiss entities under Article 21 of the Swiss VAT Act. For export zero-rating, an entity may elect to apply for the simplified VAT lump-sum tax deduction method. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; Switzerland applies mandatory hybrid mismatch rules consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide taxable turnover from taxable supplies in Switzerland, excluding exempt supplies; for non-resident entities, a lower threshold of CHF 100,000 applies to Swiss-source supplies; registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded, with voluntary registration permitted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory e-invoicing system exists for domestic VAT. Switzerland permits electronic invoices (e.g., Swiss QR-bill, EDIFACT, XML) subject to the general invoicing requirements under Article 26 of the Swiss VAT Act (must include: seller name, UID/VAT number, recipient, date, supply description, consideration, applicable tax rate, and tax amount). Since 2024, the Swiss QR-Invoice is mandatory for QR-bill payments, but not for all invoices. There is no government-run clearance/API stamping; taxpayers retain invoices for 10 years and must submit periodic VAT returns electronically through the ESTV's e-service portal or approved third-party software using the Swiss e-dec (SecureWin) transport mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: zero-rated when goods are exported to a foreign country or to a bonded warehouse/tax-free zone, provided the exporter or the recipient transfers the goods out of Switzerland; proof of export must be substantiated. Services: zero-rated for services directly related to export goods (including transport, logistics, insurance, commissioning) and for services to recipients abroad if the place of supply is outside Switzerland; Swiss payroll SaaS services to non-resident clients are generally zero-rated as intangible services if the recipient's place of business is abroad (Article 8(2) VAT Act), subject to the recipient being an entrepreneur and the service not being used in Switzerland. A written confirmation from the foreign recipient is required for the application of the reverse-charge/zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / déclaration en douane d'exportation) — e-dec export or NCTS
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR (international transport document)
Commercial invoice with export reference and Swiss seller VAT number
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of consideration from abroad (recommended for audit substantiation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the taxpayer fails to prove the export or the recipient's foreign status within 60 days of a request during an audit, the claimed zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back with interest. Fraudulent VAT evasion (including deliberate misapplication of zero-rating) is a criminal offense under Article 61 of the Swiss VAT Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and/or a fine up to CHF 30,000 (tax penalty up to 3 times the tax evaded). Negligent tax evasion carries penalties up to 3 times the tax evaded; in addition, late-payment interest accrues at 3-4% annually. The Federal Tax Administration can also impose a procedural penalty of up to CHF 10,000 for failure to maintain adequate export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Swiss Franc (CHF) is freely tradable with no exchange controls, no balance-of-payment restrictions, and no requirement for central bank approval on cross-border remittances. Profit repatriation, dividend distribution, and liquidation proceeds are freely transferable, subject only to withholding tax (35% dividends) which may be reduced under applicable tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no legal duty to surrender or repatriate export proceeds. There is no statutory conversion timeline or minimum conversion ratio. Export receipts may be held in any convertible currency and employed freely for liquidity, hedging, or reinvestment purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium. Offshore non-Swiss EMIs cannot passport into Switzerland under an EU/EEA licence. A FINMA-licensed payment institution or a Swiss banking partner is mandatory. Digital EMIs may provide a PI-layer but full treasury autonomy requires active partnership with a Swiss-regulated institution; foreign EMIs face significant restrictions in opening sponsor accounts and cannot offer payroll clearing without local regulatory cover.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors or authorised signatories is generally required for corporate account opening. Alternatively, certain Tier-1 banks permit FINMA-compliant remote video identification, provided documents are apostilled and the beneficial ownership chain is fully documented. Non-resident directors should anticipate an in-person or high-rigour virtual interview plus submission of board resolutions, charter, tax identification, and source-of-wealth statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Platform may be perceived as deposit-taking or unlicensed money transmission under Art. 1a Banking Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming SaaS-only software licence and no client-fund custody; platform architecture showing disbursements directly from client accounts to beneficiary payroll; standard contract language disclaiming deposit-taking; FINMA no-licence confirmation or exemption ruling if held.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outbound cross-border payroll payments may trigger structuring or invoice-mismatch typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed payroll outsourcing agreements; per-client employment rosters; detailed invoicing with granular service fees; bank statements showing granularity and matching payroll registers; AML manual with automated velocity checks and source-of-funds verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain with non-resident parent or Zug crypto-ecosystem exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain chart with direct UBO identification; certified passports and proof of residential address; official Swiss Commercial Register excerpt; notarised declaration of no unauthorised crypto activity; Swiss legal attestation of shareholder register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient substance and economic nexus for a Swiss AG with foreign directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss registered office lease agreement; local payroll and AHV social security records; minutes of board meetings; Swiss P&L and VAT registrations; declaratory statement of actual management location in Switzerland.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection is executed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent with the corporate tax number and purpose code referencing 'Direct investment in operating capital' (SNB balance-of-payments classification). CHF, EUR, or USD wires are accepted; banks require a board resolution and shareholder loan/subscription agreement; funds must be credited to the capital escrow account before any business disbursement. Heightened ascertainment of 'know your customer''s source of funds applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payroll disbursements, the primary rails are SEPA Credit Transfer (IBAN/BIC) within SEPA zone and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA beneficiaries. Liquidity is concentrated in the operational account with sub-account segregation; SWIFT gpi provides end-to-end tracking. Commercial letters of credit (LCs) are not applicable to payroll SaaS; trade payments are settled via clean payments rather than documentary collections. Open account clearing with multilateral netting is recommended for recurring payroll across subsidiaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) technically permissible but redundant given CHF full convertibility; usually not employed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Jahresrechnung) approved by the Ordinary General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders as internal corporate organ; no filing with the Commercial Register of the canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date; up to twelve months for consolidated financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors face personal liability for unlawful delay; shareholders may petition the court to convene the meeting; omission of required records may constitute a criminal offense under Swiss insolvency and criminal law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Federal, Cantonal and Municipal Income Tax Return (Steuererklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration acting for the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and local municipal tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal rule, generally within six months after the end of the fiscal year; extensions available upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 10–30% of assessed tax, penal interest, and possible administrative fines under the Federal Direct Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Capital Tax Return and Net Equity Confirmation (Kapitalsteuererklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year based deadline aligned with the cantonal income tax return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty interest on undeclared capital tax; reassessment within statutory limitation periods; disciplinary fines for false or incomplete disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax (MWST) Settlement Return for federal VAT-liable companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration ESTV, VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT settlement period; quarterly or annually depending on the official VAT qualification and declaration cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest accrues on late payment; late-filing administrative fine imposed; persistent failure can result in tax-recovery proceedings and forced collection measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full independent audit is compulsory for two consecutive financial years if the company exceeds at least two of three thresholds: total assets CHF 20 million, gross revenue CHF 40 million, or average 250 full-time employees. Below these thresholds a limited statutory audit is required; the shareholders may unanimously opt out of any audit subject to the absence of minority shareholder opposition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP (FER) directly under the Swiss Code of Obligations; IFRS permitted for group reporting and mandatory for listed companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law requires the AG to maintain an accurate register of the economically beneficial owners of registered shares, especially where bearer shares were converted or where the company is subject to enhanced transparency obligations. No public annual UBO filing exists; transfers of registered shares must be reflected in the share register and confirmed in the corporate minutes at the next annual meeting. Capital increases, capital decreases, and changes to authorised capital require public notarisation and registration in the Commercial Register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–30,000 per year for a standard full statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax statutory rate 8.5%, levied on profit after federal tax (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal, cantonal, and communal taxation in Zug is approximately 11.5% to 16% depending on profit level and local multiplier.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act incentives: participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (at least 10% shareholding or CHF 1 million participation value); patent box regime exempting up to 90% of qualifying net IP income; R&D super deduction increasing qualifying research and development expenditure by an additional 50%; notional interest deduction for finance and insurance group functions; no general statutory tax holiday but cantonal relief measures may apply for newly established economically active companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return designated in German as 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' and in French as 'Déclaration d'impôt pour personnes morales'; filed electronically through the competent cantonal tax administration portal (in this case Canton Zug Tax Office) or through certified tax software using the SwissTax/ESTV electronic filing data standard.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one joint tax return covering federal direct tax, cantonal tax, and communal tax for each ordinary fiscal year, with provisional prepayments made during the tax period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year tax period ending 31 December, the return is due no later than 30 September of the following year in most cantons; for a non-calendar fiscal year, filing is generally due within six months after the balance-sheet date; extension may be granted upon written application before the applicable deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, Swiss Business Identification Number UID, Commercial Register identification number, legal form Aktiengesellschaft, tax year end, principal activity (ISIC 6201 payroll automation SaaS), and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate Swiss seat and effective management address; if authorized by a non-resident board member, attach formal power of attorney and identification documentation of the foreign ultimate beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 2 - Balance sheet and income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial balance sheet at the beginning and end of the tax period, statutory income statement, net turnover from payroll SaaS subscriptions and implementation services, personnel expenses, depreciation, amortization, and financial results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intercompany balances, receivables, payables, loans, license fees, and management service charges with foreign related parties; state the functional currency if the books are not maintained in CHF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions for non-deductible expenses such as withholding tax, capital tax, tax penalties, excessive depreciation, and hidden profit distributions; deductions for participation exemption, patent box relief, R&D super deduction, notional interest deduction, and tax-exempt reorganization gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach transfer-pricing documentation, patent box qualification reports, R&D project records, and notional interest deduction calculations so that requests for deduction are substantiated for the non-resident-owned structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 4 - Computation of taxable profit and capital tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit for federal and cantonal purposes after applying loss carryforwards and all legal deductions; cantonal capital tax is based on net taxable equity and must be reported in the same return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty exemptions or foreign-sourced income exclusions only through the return and supporting schedules; no blanket exemption arises from foreign ownership; Swiss tax residence of the AG must be supported by actual management presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 5 - Withholding tax reconciliation and distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of dividends declared, distributions in kind, interest paid on Swiss debt instruments, shareholders, beneficial owners, amount of Swiss federal withholding tax withheld, payment dates, and reference to the corresponding withholding tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report distributions to non-resident beneficial owners with country of residence, shareholding percentage, and DTA application; the 35% Swiss withholding tax must have been withheld and remitted before any treaty refund may be requested by the shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory audit report, detailed tax reconciliation, group organization chart, transfer-pricing master file and local file, country-by-country notification, patent box and R&D evidence, depreciation schedules, and shareholder register extracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned AGs should attach beneficial ownership declarations and, where applicable, an OECD residence certificate for foreign shareholders; provide Swiss payroll substance evidence such as employment records and office lease.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers procedural fines under Article 174 of the Federal Direct Tax Act, generally up to CHF 10,000, plus tax authority estimated assessment, enforced collection, and statutory late-payment interest; wilful non-filing or false filing may escalate to criminal tax proceedings with significantly higher penalties and personal liability for responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions; no further cantonal dividend withholding tax; reduced rates apply only by treaty or statutory restitution procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss paying company must withhold 35% at source and remit the amount to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration on the prescribed withholding tax return. A non-resident shareholder seeking treaty relief must file a claim with the Federal Tax Administration using the official refund application form, accompanied by an official certificate of residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home-country tax authority, beneficial ownership declaration, a statement of shareholding period, and, where required, documentary evidence of entitlement under the applicable double taxation agreement. Refund of the portion of the 35% withholding exceeding the treaty rate is generally applied to the non-resident shareholder by the Federal Tax Administration; the paying company cannot independently apply the reduced treaty rate at source without an applicable domestic exemption, advanced ruling, or FTA procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 35% on dividends and on interest from Swiss-resident debt instruments and certain Swiss bank deposit interest; royalties have no Swiss source withholding tax. Treaty rates for interest are commonly 0% to 10%, depending on the recipients and type of debt claim; royalties are commonly 0% under Swiss double tax treaties. All treaty reductions require proof of beneficial ownership and, for interest, a residence certificate; Swiss withholding tax remains payable in the first instance unless a domestic exemption applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss federal law does not prescribe a statutory monetary threshold for Local File or Master File documentation. In practice, the Swiss tax administration expects contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation when intercompany transactions are material, including intragroup royalties, management fees, software licensing, and financing. Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated turnover of at least CHF 900 million. A Swiss AG with smaller revenue must still demonstrate arm's-length behavior through a local file, benchmarking study, or functional analysis whenever transactions with foreign related parties exceed ordinary commercial scale.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no separate Economic Substance Regulation in the form used by some low-tax jurisdictions, but Swiss tax law, jurisprudence, and treaty-abuse doctrines require real economic substance for corporate tax residence, treaty eligibility, and preferential tax regimes. A Swiss AG must have a valid registered office, actual decision-making management in Switzerland, substantive board meetings, employees performing payroll and software development functions, books and records kept in Switzerland, and business purpose. The patent box, notional interest deduction, and participation exemption can be denied if the company lacks local substance or is used as a letterbox.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false corporate income tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly suppressing Swiss payroll SaaS subscription revenue, generating false invoices, fabricating deductible R&D expenditures, booking personal expenses as company deductions, or repeatedly failing to file the corporate income tax return with intent to evade federal and cantonal taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of suppressed profit, late-payment interest, and administrative tax penalty in an amount generally equal to or exceeding the tax evaded; under the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act, wilful tax evasion may be prosecuted as tax fraud and is punishable by a monetary criminal penalty and imprisonment in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false returns or caused the company to evade taxes face direct civil liability under Article 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, personal orders for restitution of evaded taxes, travel bans, disqualification from board service, and custodial sanctions where tax fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and sham intercompany arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties or management fees to the Swiss payroll AG, allocating excessive profit to a foreign affiliate without employees or functions, failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, or structuring circular software licences solely to shift profit to unrelated low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment by the tax authority, disallowance of excessive deductions, additional tax assessment, penalty interest, procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 for missing documentation, and potential criminal tax penalties in cases involving fabricated intercompany agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute backdated or fictitious agreements face personal liability for resulting tax losses, exclusion from business travel and board mandates during criminal proceedings, confiscation of bonuses connected to the arrangement, and imprisonment for involvement in tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Violation of Swiss withholding tax obligations on dividend and interest repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident parent without withholding the statutory 35% Swiss federal withholding tax, classifying distributions as intercompany services or loans to avoid the dividend article, or failing to report interest on Swiss debt instruments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may issue a formal demand against the company for 35% of the gross distribution plus interest, impose penalty for non-withholding or late remittance, and refuse deduction of penalties; deliberate non-declaration is treated as criminal tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and executives are jointly and severally liable with the company for unpaid withholding tax if they knowingly instructed or tolerated non-compliance, and may be subject to personal restitution orders, asset freezing, bank travel restrictions, and criminal imprisonment in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company abuse and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an existing dormant Swiss shell AG, changing ownership and purpose without a capital increase or new commercial substance, maintaining no employees, no office, no Swiss bank accounts, no board meetings in Switzerland, or otherwise using the AG as a pure conduit to access Swiss treaty benefits and international payroll payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Commercial Register and tax authorities may disregard the shell acquisition, retroactively reclassify the transaction as a liquidation and re-establishment, deny treaty benefits, impose capital-formation obligations, levy fines for false declarations, and in severe cases order ex officio dissolution of the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the de facto beneficial owner who used the shell as their personal instrument face veil piercing, personal civil restitution of hidden assets, travel bans, revocation of commercial signatory rights, and imprisonment for criminal falsification of tax and commercial register documents.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and payment-rail compliance violations in payroll automation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG payroll SaaS infrastructure to move payroll and client funds through Swift and direct-debit rails without adequate anti-money-laundering controls, serving sanctioned entities, processing payroll linked to corruption or human-trafficking proceeds, deliberately failing to report suspicious transactions to MROS, or operating as an unlicensed payment intermediary in excess of permissible ancillary business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enforcement action by FINMA, referral to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office, confiscation of illegal assets, administrative fines, criminal fines up to CHF 500,000 under Articles 305bis and 305ter of the Swiss Criminal Code, and prohibition from engaging in financial-market activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the board and management who consciously enable illicit payment flows are personally liable for breaches of Swiss criminal law, may be ordered to pay civil restitution to the company or clients, face travel bans and custodial sentences up to three years or more for qualified money laundering, and may be banned from any future management role in financial or payment businesses.
